profile.reading:
Per QTS's own facility page, Santa Clara 2 shares the 4-acre multi-building campus at 2805 Mission College Boulevard, Santa Clara, CA 95054 with sibling building Santa Clara 1; QTS's page is structured around Santa Clara 1 specifically (giving that building 7.5 MW) and does not separately publish a capacity or sqft figure for the distinct Santa Clara 2 building. The campus carries Energy Star and LEED Silver certification, seismic protection for customer equipment, and on-site EV charging.

QTS was founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas, and was taken private in a roughly $10 billion Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust (BREIT)-led acquisition completed August 31, 2021, per Blackstone's own press release; QTS is no longer an independent SEC filer.

QTS positions itself as a "hyperscale-neutral" wholesale and colocation landlord, leasing built data center capacity to enterprise, cloud, and hyperscale tenants rather than operating its own end-user cloud service, a business model it shares with peers such as Digital Realty and CyrusOne. Since Blackstone completed its roughly $10 billion take-private acquisition in August 2021, QTS has continued expanding across multiple US metros rather than slowing development, including major campus filings and expansions in Phoenix (a 750MW, 375-acre Glendale campus acquired for $255.3 million in July 2022) and Dallas-Fort Worth (its two mega-scale Irving and Fort Worth campuses), consistent with the scale of buildout QTS has also pursued in Northern Virginia, Georgia, and Ohio, tracked elsewhere in this registry.

QTS was originally founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas by Chad Williams, and grew through a mix of acquisitions and ground-up construction into a national wholesale/colocation platform before its 2013 IPO as a publicly traded REIT; that public period ended with the 2021 Blackstone take-private deal. QTS's current published portfolio language describes over 30 facilities across North America and Europe on its own site, while Wikipedia gives a somewhat different approximate figure of 28 locations across 16 US states plus two Netherlands sites (Eemshaven and Groningen), a discrepancy this registry notes rather than resolves in favor of either source.

reading.body:
QTS Santa Clara 2 publishes 7.5 MW of IT capacity across a multi-building campus on Mission College Boulevard in Santa Clara, California, though the operator does not separately specify which buildings comprise this facility or break out distinct capacity figures between Santa Clara 1 and Santa Clara 2.

At 40 kW per rack, a density typical of AI training workloads, 7.5 MW supports roughly 188 racks. At 10 kW per rack, a colocation baseline, it supports roughly 750 racks. These are calculations based on assumed rack density, not operator claims about actual configuration. The campus holds Energy Star and LEED Silver certification, meaning it meets recognized standards for energy efficiency in construction and operation. The operator page publishes no uptime tier, power redundancy specification, or connectivity detail.

Among 103 mapped facilities in California, only seven publish a megawatt figure. QTS Santa Clara 2 ranks fourth among those seven, representing roughly 4 percent of the 185 MW this site has recorded statewide. This ranking is fragile. The gap between mapped facilities and those with published data means the true California total is almost certainly larger, and this facility's standing could shift significantly as more operators disclose capacity.

For AI workload evaluation, 7.5 MW is moderate by current hyperscale standards, where single training clusters regularly consume tens of megawatts or more. LEED certification addresses building efficiency and environmental design, not the power delivery density or fiber connectivity that AI clusters depend on most. Whether this campus hosts GPU clusters, how its power architecture is designed, or how it connects to the grid remain unpublished, requiring direct operator inquiry.
